chunks: Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj, from Bishr ibn Ja'far, from Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said:

I heard him saying, 'Do you know what the shirt of Yusuf (عليه السلام) was?' He said: I said, 'No.' He said: 'When the fire was kindled for Ibrahim (عليه السلام), Jibra'il (عليه السلام) came to him with a garment from the garments of Paradise and clothed him with it, so neither heat nor cold harmed him while it was with him.'

Then when death came before Ibrahim, he placed it in an amulet and hung it upon Ishaq, and Ishaq hung it upon Ya'qub. Then when Yusuf (عليه السلام) was born, he hung it upon him, and it remained on his upper arm until there occurred of his affair what occurred. Then when Yusuf brought it out from the amulet in Egypt, Ya'qub sensed its scent.
And it is His saying: 'Indeed, I surely find the scent of Yusuf, were it not that you would deem me senile.'
So that was the shirt which Allah sent down from Paradise.

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, then to whom did that shirt pass?' He said, 'To its people.' Then he said, 'Every Prophet who left inherited knowledge or something else, it has indeed ended up with the family of Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله).'

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The family of Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), described as the final inheritors of prophetic legacy.
key_terms.تَمِيمَةٍ: An amulet or protective wrapping in which the garment was placed.
key_terms.ثِيَابِ الْجَنَّةِ: Garments of Paradise, indicating the shirt's celestial origin.
key_terms.رِيحَ يُوسُفَ: The scent of Yusuf (عليه السلام) perceived by Ya'qub (عليه السلام).
key_terms.قَمِيصُ يُوسُفَ: The shirt of Yusuf (عليه السلام), identified here as a heavenly garment passed down through prophets.

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the shirt of Yusuf (عليه السلام) and how did it reach آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ (صلى الله عليه وآله)?
ai.summary: This narration explains that the shirt associated with Yusuf (عليه السلام) was originally a garment from Paradise given to Ibrahim (عليه السلام) and passed down through the prophets until it reached Yusuf (عليه السلام). It also connects the scent perceived by Ya'qub (عليه السلام) to that heavenly garment and concludes that the inherited knowledge and relics of the prophets ultimately came to آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ (صلى الله عليه وآله).
